newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Some Russian MinFins set records but trade thin.
newsitem.headline: Some Russian MinFins set records but trade thin.

text.p: Some Russian MinFin bonds set records pushed up by an overnight rise in U.S. Treauries in otherwise thin trading due to U.S. Independence Day holiday, dealers said on Friday.
All tranches, except the shortest one, hit new all-time records for the second consecutive day.
"Prices rose again as (U.S.) Treasuries rose yesterday but trading is not active de to their holiday," Avtobank dealer Ivan Kuznetsov said.
Dealers said active trading had stopped at midday, with many Western players stepping outside until Monday on the day-off of their U.S. counterparties.
They added prices were likely to be steady at current levels, with profit-taking possible after the rise of up to two points over the recent week.
The Labour Department said on Thursday 217,000 overall non-farm jobs were added to payrolls in June, up from 166,000 new jobs in May.
The key 30-year U.S. Treasury bond gained more than a full point late on Thursday and its yield slumped to 6.61 percent from 6.71 percent on Wednesday.
MinFins, along with other emerging debt, are sensitive to any news suggesting a change in U.S. interest rates and U.S. Treasury bond prices.
